Export the subscription Activity Log to a storage account in this environment (the destination must exist).
s:
az monitor diagnostic-settings subscription create --name actlog --location global \
  --storage-account /subscriptions/00000000-0000-0000-0000-cloudlearn01/resourceGroups/my-rg/providers/Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/mystorage \
  --logs '[{"category":"Administrative","enabled":true}]'

import requests

r = requests.put("{EP}/subscriptions/00000000-0000-0000-0000-cloudlearn01/providers/Microsoft.Insights/diagnosticSettings/actlog?api-version=2021-05-01-preview",
    headers={"Authorization": "Bearer dev"},
    json={"properties": {"storageAccountId": "/subscriptions/00000000-0000-0000-0000-cloudlearn01/resourceGroups/my-rg/providers/Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/mystorage", "logs": [{"category": "Administrative", "enabled": true}, {"category": "Security", "enabled": true}]}})
print(r.status_code, r.json() if r.content else "")

features.t: Alert rules (metric + activity log alert rules: create, list, delete)
Action groups (create, list, delete, test notification, enable receiver)

x: Scaling never actually runs (there is no live metric stream to evaluate rules against); the setting is stored and returned exactly as configured.

features.t: Activity log (subscription-wide feed of real ARM writes)
x: Only control-plane writes Vyomi itself performs are recorded; there is no data-plane or sign-in activity.

features.t: Log Analytics workspaces (create, list, delete, keys, usage, tables)
Per-resource-type Insights dashboards (Applications, Virtual Machines, Storage accounts, Networks, Azure Cosmos DB, Key Vaults, Service Bus)
x: Shows Vyomi's real resource inventory for the type; there is no request/exception/dependency telemetry, VM guest metrics, or health rollup — those need an agent-based collection pipeline Vyomi does not run.
Scope, resource-type and location pickers are real (drawn from your inventory); the chart itself is not — metric definitions/values are not modelled.

features.t: Monitoring Coverage (resources with vs. without an alert rule)
x: Coverage is approximated as "referenced by at least one alert rule's scopes"; Azure's own per-signal telemetry coverage model is not reproduced.

features.t: Advisor recommendations (resources with no alert rule, derived from real inventory)
x: Recommendations are "this resource has no alert rule", not Azure Advisor's own usage-pattern heuristics.

features.t: Metrics charts (metric definitions and time-series values)
x: Exactly one real metric exists per resource — "Activity operations", a genuine count of that resource's own Activity log rows (never synthetic/random data), bucketed over the requested interval.

Only a small KQL subset is understood: a table name, then any of where (==/!=/contains/startswith), project, sort by/order by, take/limit and count — unsupported syntax returns a real error instead of succeeding silently.

Modelled as the real mechanic behind it — a Microsoft.Insights/dataCollectionRuleAssociations extension resource linking a VM to an existing Data Collection Rule, validated against the shared ARM store — rather than a cosmetic "agent installed" flag.

Vyomi has no cross-signal (metrics + logs + availability) ML correlation engine; this groups the one real failure signal the backend produces — Activity log rows whose status isn't Succeeded — by resource.

A health model is real CRUD (Microsoft.Insights/healthModels: a named collection of member resource ids); the rollup health per member is computed from the same real Activity-log failure signal Issues uses, not authored dependency/signal graphs with weighted health criteria the real feature supports.

features.t: Change Analysis (derived from the real Activity log)
x: Change type/Name/Resource type are derived from the Activity log feed (real ARM writes), not from Azure Resource Graph's property-level snapshots — there is no before/after diff of individual properties.

There is no real Azure platform behind Vyomi to go down, so a fabricated incident feed would be dishonest. Instead this lists the REAL resource provider namespaces this subscription has registered (GET /subscriptions/{sub}/providers) — every one Available, which is a true statement about this environment (no fault injection), not a canned incident list.
A workbook is stored as a name/category/serializedData document, the same shape the real resource has; there is no visual report editor to author the serializedData JSON.

Lists real Grafana workspaces and renders one built-in dashboard of Vyomi's real Activity-log operations (by resource type and per hour) itself. It is not Grafana, and saved/favourite Grafana dashboards are not modelled.

Shows Vyomi's real AKS cluster inventory (Microsoft.ContainerService/managedClusters, the same core/azure_arm_core.py store the AKS console reads); there is no container/pod-level telemetry or log collection — that needs an agent-based collection pipeline Vyomi does not run.

Microsoft.Cache/redis is a real, generic-catalog ARM resource (control plane only — the cache instance, SKU and access keys behave like Azure); this page shows that real inventory, not a telemetry rollup (there is no Redis data-plane protocol server behind it).

Microsoft.Kusto/clusters is a real, generic-catalog ARM resource (control plane only — the cluster resource, SKU and state behave like Azure); this page shows that real inventory, not a telemetry rollup (there is no Kusto query engine behind it).
Azure Local (hybrid hardware) is out of scope for a cloud simulator.

Microsoft.Monitor/accounts is a real ARM resource: name rules, query endpoint, and the managed data collection endpoint and rule Azure creates alongside it (removed again on delete; deleting a workspace still integrated with a Grafana workspace is refused).

Microsoft.Dashboard/grafana is a real ARM resource: name, SKU and major-version validation, generated endpoint, system identity, and Azure Monitor workspace integrations validated against real Azure Monitor workspaces.
SCOM managed instance is out of scope for a simulator.

features.t: Diagnostic settings (per-resource logs/metrics routing: resource picker + create/list/delete)
x: Logs/metrics are never actually delivered to the configured destination (workspace, storage account or event hub) — there is no agent/telemetry pipeline, so the setting is stored and validated exactly as the real resource requires but nothing flows.
A rule's data flows and destinations are stored and validated exactly as the real resource requires; data is never actually collected or routed (there is no agent fleet to configure).
The logs/metrics/configuration ingestion endpoint URLs are generated and stable across updates, the same shape the real resource returns; nothing is ever sent to them (no agent fleet).

A pipeline group's platform and collector endpoints are stored and validated exactly as the real resource requires (Microsoft.Insights/pipelineGroups); no on-premises OpenTelemetry collector fleet actually runs, so nothing is ever collected or forwarded — the same "config real, data flow not" shape as Data Collection Endpoints.

features.t: Azure Monitor Private Link Scopes (create, list, delete, access mode settings, Azure Monitor Resources)
x: The scope resource, its query/ingestion access-mode settings and its scoped resources (the "Azure Monitor Resources" tab — linking a Log Analytics workspace into the scope) are real and validated against the shared inventory; private endpoint connections are not modelled — Vyomi has no private networking stack.

features.t: Fired alerts (metric, activity log and log-search rules evaluated for real; change state; history; summary)
x: Rules are evaluated when alerts are read or via the evaluate action - there is no background timer on Nano.

features.t: Alert processing rules (suppress notifications, add action groups; scope, condition and schedule enforced)
Prometheus rule groups (ARM resource + rule validation)
x: Rule groups are validated (PromQL syntax) and EVALUATED (core/azure_promql.py): recording rules append new series to the Azure Monitor workspace's sample store, alert rules fire after their `for` duration through the shared alert pipeline (alerts list, action-group webhooks) and auto-resolve. PromQL subset: selectors with matchers, rate/irate/increase/delta/*_over_time/abs/ceil/floor/round/clamp/vector/absent/scalar, sum/avg/min/max/count/group/stddev/topk/bottomk by/without, binary arithmetic/comparison (bool) and and/or/unless with on/ignoring; no subqueries, histogram_quantile, label_replace or group_left/right. Samples enter through POST providers/Microsoft.AlertsManagement/vyomiProm/ingest (remote-write style) -- nothing scrapes targets.

features.t: Log search alert rules (scheduledQueryRules evaluated by the Log Analytics KQL engine)
x: The KQL engine supports where/extend/project/summarize/top/order/take/count/distinct, not joins, unions, let or time-series functions.

features.t: Resources collecting through a data collection rule (association list)
Alert timeline (fired/resolved/state-change events from real alert history)
